title: video_player
objectives: Understand video_player via a real-life analogy
Configure controllers for network / asset / file / HLS-DASH
Choose between video_player, chewie, better_player, media_kit

sections.markdown:
**Think of `video_player` as a bare-metal DVD player + a TV cable.**

A DVD player takes a media source, decodes video/audio, and emits frames on the TV. `video_player` is that player as a Flutter widget:

- **VideoPlayerController** — the DVD player. Load a URL / asset / file / bytes; call `play/pause/seekTo/setVolume/setPlaybackSpeed`.
- **VideoPlayer widget** — the TV screen. Wraps a `Texture` (Android) / `AVPlayerLayer` (iOS) that Flutter composites via PlatformView / Texture.
- **VideoProgressIndicator** — the seek bar with buffered + played ranges.
- **`ChewieController` (chewie package)** — the remote control (play/pause button, seek, fullscreen, subtitles). Because raw video_player has no UI beyond the frame.
- **HLS / DASH** — video_player supports HLS on iOS natively + on Android via ExoPlayer's HLS extension. For DASH + DRM + subtitles you generally need `better_player` or `media_kit`.

**Why every media-heavy Flutter app uses this or its wrappers:** it's the official Flutter team package; wraps ExoPlayer (Android) + AVPlayer (iOS) — the same engines native apps use. Solid enough for TikTok-style scrolling feeds if you tune preloading. For richer needs (DRM, adaptive quality UI, chapters, advanced subtitles) reach for `better_player` or `media_kit`.

**`video_player`** (`^2.x`, official Flutter team plugin) wraps ExoPlayer (Android), AVPlayer (iOS), and the browser's `<video>` on Web. **Controllers**: `.network(url)`, `.asset(path)`, `.file(file)`, `.contentUri(uri)`. State exposed via `ValueListenable<VideoPlayerValue>` (position, duration, buffered, isPlaying, aspectRatio, hasError). Provides the frame + basic playback controls; you build the UI. Wrappers: **`chewie`** (Material/Cupertino default controls), **`better_player`** (subtitles + DRM + PiP), **`media_kit`** (libmpv-based, most-capable + heavier).

sections.markdown: ## Full setup — network video with custom controls
## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Not disposing controller.** Video decoders hold native memory + surfaces; leaving one alive after screen leaves = memory bloat + audio ghost. Always dispose.
**Mistake 2: Building `VideoPlayer` widget before `initialize()` completes.** Blank frame + errors. Guard on `controller.value.isInitialized`.

**Mistake 3: Instantiating multiple controllers in a scrollable feed.** Each holds native decoder; 20 controllers = OOM. Reuse one controller + swap sources, or use `pod_player`-style page controllers.
**Mistake 4: Ignoring lifecycle.** Audio keeps playing when app backgrounds; battery drain. Wire `WidgetsBindingObserver` → pause on paused.
**Mistake 5: Full-res 4K on cellular.** Bandwidth + battery. Use adaptive streaming (HLS/DASH) with quality tiers.
**Mistake 6: No error UI.** Network hiccups + expired signed URLs happen. Listen for `.hasError` + show retry.
**Mistake 7: Preloading too much.** Preloading 10 videos = huge network + memory. Preload 1-2 next tiles.
**Mistake 8: Missing manifest / Info.plist entries** for `usesCleartextTraffic` (Android) or `NSAppTransportSecurity` (iOS) when testing HTTP videos in dev.
## Best practices
**1. `dispose()` in `State.dispose`.** Non-negotiable.
**2. Pause on background.** Wire lifecycle observer.
**3. Adaptive streaming** — serve HLS / DASH; player auto-selects quality.
**4. Preload just-in-time** (1-2 next tiles).
**5. Error listener** — surface retry UI.
**6. `chewie` for standard UI** — don't reinvent controls.
**7. `better_player` for streaming apps** — DRM, subtitles, adaptive quality UI.
**8. Sound with `mixWithOthers` when appropriate** — avoid interrupting user music.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Network video with play/pause + seek.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Custom controls: seek bar + skip 10 s + speed.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Lifecycle: pause on background + resume on foreground.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Vertical PageView feed with 1-controller reuse across pages.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — HLS stream + adaptive quality via better_player.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Native PiP mode integration + fullscreen support.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What does `video_player` wrap and what are the platform trade-offs?**

**A:** **Android:** ExoPlayer (Google's official player), full HLS + DASH + WebM + progressive downloads. **iOS:** AVPlayer (Apple's native), HLS + progressive; DASH via HLS-only route. **Web:** browser `<video>` element; supports the codecs the browser supports; HLS on Safari only natively (need `hls.js` on Chrome). **Desktop:** limited support; `media_kit` (libmpv) is the desktop-first alternative. **Trade-offs:** consistent Flutter API but format support differs by platform — on iOS you cannot easily play DASH; on Web you must feature-detect. **Latency:** initial load takes 200-800 ms for network sources; assets are fast. **DRM:** not supported in bare video_player; use better_player for Widevine (Android) + FairPlay (iOS).

**Q2: How do you build a TikTok-style scrolling video feed efficiently?**

**A:** **The trap:** creating one `VideoPlayerController` per page in a PageView.builder = 20+ native decoders alive = OOM crash. **Pattern:** limited controller pool. Options: **(1) 3-controller ring** — current + previous + next; each page uses one; on swipe, evict the oldest, initialize the newer one. **(2) `pod_player`/`chewie`** with a single controller reused; swap source on page change. **(3) Preload thumbnails, not video** — show a poster until the user pauses on a page for > 100 ms, then start playback. **(4) Pause when the tile leaves viewport** — `VisibilityDetector` package fires callbacks. **(5) Reset controller on huge memory pressure** — listen for `MemoryPressureNotification`. **(6) Auto-play + tap-to-mute** — TikTok UX. **Interviewer signal:** knowing the controller pool trick separates candidates who've shipped video feeds from those who've prototyped.

**Q3: When would you pick `chewie` / `better_player` / `media_kit` over bare `video_player`?**

**A:** **Bare `video_player`** — custom UX (branded controls, in-video overlays, in-context play buttons); tight control over play/pause via app logic. **`chewie`** — standard Material or Cupertino controls with fullscreen + volume + speed. Zero custom code; ideal for internal / prototype / simple playback screens. **`better_player`** — streaming media apps: adaptive HLS/DASH with quality menus, subtitles (SRT/VTT), DRM (Widevine / FairPlay), PiP mode, Chromecast. Solid for VOD services. **`media_kit`** — libmpv under the hood; supports every codec + subtitle format; best for desktop targets (Windows / Linux) or when you need exotic formats. Larger binary (~15 MB per platform). **Rule:** start with `video_player`; add `chewie` for standard controls; upgrade to `better_player` for streaming apps; `media_kit` for desktop / niche needs.

**Q4: How do you handle lifecycle correctly?**

**A:** Video controllers survive `dispose` only if YOU dispose them — otherwise they leak. **(1) `WidgetsBindingObserver.didChangeAppLifecycleState`** — pause on `paused` (screen locked / app backgrounded); resume behavior depends on UX (auto-resume vs stay-paused). **(2) Screen-off / call-received** on Android/iOS also triggers `paused`. **(3) In a list, `VisibilityDetector` listens for scroll-off** — pause. **(4) Route pop with `willPop`** — dispose before the route unmounts. **(5) Background audio** — if you want to keep audio playing (like YouTube), enable `mixWithOthers` + configure the audio session; also declare `audio` in iOS background modes. **(6) On foreground return** — restore position via `controller.value.position` if that matters. **(7) Memory pressure** — dispose off-screen controllers proactively. **Interviewers score highly on candidates who mention audio session + background modes.**

**Q5: How do you support subtitles + DRM?**

**A:** Bare `video_player` doesn't natively handle either. **Subtitles:** use `better_player` with `subtitles` property (SRT / VTT / TXT); or overlay text yourself via a stream of position events. Native HLS streams can carry subtitles inline (WebVTT tracks) which `AVPlayer` / `ExoPlayer` render automatically. **DRM:** **Widevine** on Android (via ExoPlayer's DrmSessionManager), **FairPlay** on iOS (via AVFoundation content-key session). `better_player` exposes both; setup: license URL + optional headers; DRM tokens usually fetched from your DRM service. **Testing DRM** is a nightmare — production-signed tokens only work on real devices. **Alternative: hosted-player embeds** — some vendors (Mux, Cloudflare Stream) provide their own Flutter SDK with DRM baked in; considerably less work than DIY.

**Q6: How do you keep video costs under control at consumer scale?**

**A:** **(1) Adaptive streaming (HLS/DASH)** — serve multiple bitrates; player auto-selects based on bandwidth. Users on 3G get 480p; wifi users get 1080p. Saves 5-10× bandwidth. **(2) CDN with regional pops** — Cloudflare Stream, AWS CloudFront, GCP CDN. Latency + cost. **(3) Preload economics** — don't fetch full videos; fetch manifests + first segments. **(4) Cache locally** — HLS segments; short TTL for freshness. **(5) Feed monetization** — pre-roll ads compensate for delivery; measure Ad-View-Through vs bandwidth. **(6) Codec choice** — H.264 (universal) vs H.265 / HEVC (30 % smaller, license fees) vs AV1 (50 % smaller, patent-free but slower encode). **(7) Poster thumbnails** — avoid loading video until user taps. **(8) Analytics on completion rates** — a 10 % completion means most people don't watch; consider shorter forms. **CDN bill is often the #1 line item for video apps; every optimization counts.**

## Real-world usage

- **Short-form vertical feeds** (TikTok, Instagram Reels clones).
- **Product demos** (auto-play muted; unmute on tap).
- **Educational lectures** — speed control, chapters, subtitles.
- **Live streams** — HLS with < 30 s latency.
- **NOT ideal for** — real-time video calling (use WebRTC / Agora / Twilio); AR / heavy editing.

## Advanced notes

- **`VideoPlayerOptions(mixWithOthers: true)`** — don't stop the user's music.
- **`setPlaybackSpeed(1.5)`** — variable playback speed.
- **`ClosedCaptionFile`** — attach a VTT/SRT.
- **Audio session config on iOS** — `AVAudioSessionCategoryPlayback` for background audio.
- **PiP** — needs native config + `better_player` provides Dart APIs.
- **Fullscreen** — flip status bar + orientation via `SystemChrome`; wrap in `RotatedBox` for landscape.
- **`AudioSession`** package for advanced audio focus handling.
- **Frame accurate seek** — `seekTo(Duration(microseconds: ...))` — some codecs snap to keyframes.
- **HLS manifest tuning** — segment length (2-4 s standard), target duration.
- **Video ads (VAST / VMAP)** — separate SDK (Google IMA).
- **Screen recording detection** — `flutter_windowmanager` (Android) / `UIScreen.isCaptured` (iOS) — some apps block playback while recording.
- **Screenshot protection** for DRM content — Android FLAG_SECURE, iOS masking on `UIApplicationWillResignActive`.
